Those who are His co-actors appear as parents of this world, who in pleasure and pain exhaust themselves for His sake, as if He were a child, in its helplessness in need of his parents.

He and His Play are always transcendental, even when He gives Himself out as being of this world. He and those who belong to Him are always formed of Being, Knowledge and Bliss and never become human beings of flesh and blood. Only deceived fools think that Krsna has a body consisting of Maya, that He is born like a human child and is a slave to the laws of our world.

He and His play with His Own co-actors are not an idealization of the world, formed by ignorance; His Play is a derision, an insult to the world and people’s relations to each other. Man’s love for his children is like a travesty of the Divine parents’ genuine love for the Divine Child. When He and His Own co-actors play in this lila on earth, in shapes, whose distorted shadows are the Maya-begotten men of this world, He and His Own co-actors experience a special, intensified form of Bliss. Just as His Own co-actors only breathe and exist for His sake, He exists and plays only for their sake and for their happiness. Their happiness and consequently His Own happiness intensify in the lila that becomes visible in the world.

The sastrams tell about this lila and do it in such a way that it gives an insight into God’s inner life. But just as no one, except those who are His Own co-actors, are able to experience the true lila - its appearances and the fact that man has turned his back on God conceal it - no one is able to understand the statements of the sastrams, who is not willing, at least, in serving, knowing devotion, to let himself be enlightened by the sastrams. The purpose of this act of listening to the Damodara-lila is not to satisfy man’s craving for knowledge, but, in the heart of those who want to serve it may awaken the desire, through God’s and His Own co-actors’ Grace, in a future life, to be a particle of dust under the feet of His Own co-actors (Bha X. 14,34), or one day be allowed to serve those, who already serve Him since eternity (Bha X.87,23).

5

The Damodara-lila is subject of inner reflection of all those, who are filled with the unflinching confidence, that the serving, knowing Love for Krsna is the path as well as the goal, the eternal fulfilment of the aim of the atma in the eternal kingdom of God.

One whole month a year, the bhaktas, those who are dedicated to God, reflect upon, celebrate and discuss this Damodara-lila. This is the reason why this month is called “Damodara”. Those who have turned their backs on God call this month “Karttika”.

The following rendering of the Damodara-lila presents the statements of this lila in Bhagavatam, Gopala-Campu and Ananda-Vrndavana-Campu. The introduction preceding this presentation, must be thoroughly thought-out, understood and unceasingly kept in mind. The greatest possible danger is to regard this Damodara-lila with the eyes of a mother or a father of this human world or in dismal abandonment of God even mentally or emotionally want to place oneself in the role of a Nanda or a Yasoda. Man as such, however noble and fine, may never think -even in the most pious imagination - that he, with his individual I, could try to force himself near to one of His Own co-actors or even Krsna Himself. The highest value of man lies in his end in the transition from abandonment of God to dedication to the power of serving, knowing Love. This Love prays for the gift to be allowed, through one’s ears, heart and thoughts, to serve the eternal parents by intent *listening* and a *versatile mind.*

***First Part***

When the Damodara-lila is enacted, Krsna manifests the characteristics of a child at the age of two years and a little less than two months. His father Nanda (joy) is the king of the cowherds in Vraja. His mother Yasoda (glory- and praise-giving) is the highly respected administrator of the opulent household of the cowherds. Nanda’s and Yasoda’s brothers and relations live at different places in the neighbourhood. Nanda’s house with its spacious courtyards and gardens are situated at the centre of the village Gokula. Nearby flows the deep-blue river Yamuna.

Around the spacious courtyard of the household four smaller buildings are grouped together.

To the south, towards the flower garden, which almost reaches the house, lies the house of the parents. In its western part, is the spacious room, in which Yasoda lives with Krsna, and in its eastern part lives Nanda, His father.

An elongated veranda connects the dwelling-house with the courtyard.

To the west lies the spacious storehouse: granaries in the southern part, the room for storage of soured, thick milk, fresh butter and ghi, i.e. clarified, melted butter, in the northern part. These valuable products hang in big earthenware jars, hooked on to the ceiling of the room with strong loops of rope.

To the north lies Rohini’s dwelling-house, where she usually stays together with Balarama, Krsna’s elder brother.

To the east stands the temple of Narayana, with His four-armed figure - the glorious and majestic manifestation of God. During the day He is regularly worshipped there by brahmins.

In the south-western corner of this square of buildings is the elongated kitchen, with passages to the inner courtyard, to the storehouse and to Yasoda’s living room. From the south-eastern corner of the courtyard a well-kept path leads to the south, connecting the house to the road of the village. On that spot, a little on the side of the road, there are two great trees, whose stems form a mighty “V” and almost seem to touch each other at the ground; a distinctive mark of the building of the king of the cowherds, which can be seen from a great distance. They are called Yamala-Arjuna, the famous twin trees.

The rainy season is over, it is a few days before the day of the new moon in the month of damodara. The great feast, arranged by the worshippers of Indra, the god of the clouds and the rain, is approaching. The cowherdesses, who usually find time to slip along to have a chat with Yasoda, are now busy in their own houses with the preparations for this feast. In spite of their great yearning, today they are unable to let their ears and eyes rejoice at the ever exhilarated Child’s amusing plays.

Rohini together with Balarama had been invited to Upananda, Nanda’s elder brother. They had gone to Upananda’s neighbouring village, escorted by Nanda, who then went to tend the cows.

Yasoda has many maids, young and old, who are always ready to serve her, and who want to relieve her from all kinds of chores, not only because she is their beloved mistress, but in that way they also serve Krsna, whose transcendental charm enchants them all. For Krsna’s sake they do not feel any fatigue. Krsna is their life, their strength, their joy. In the early morning, they had hastened away in order to make butter from the thick soured milk, and to boil the milk from the noble cow Padmagandha (scent of lotus) for Krsna, because this milk is meant for Him. Might there be a greater pleasure than to churn for Him and to relieve His noble mother from her chores, so that she can devote herself entirely to her Child? They are all well acquainted with every aspect of the art of housekeeping. It is the serving, knowing Love, that radiates from Him and through their hearts and hands streams back to Him. But today - in spite of the happy prayers of the maids -Yasoda is not willing to deprive herself of the happiness of churning, and preparing the milk for Him. Today she is severe. Against her better judgement, the idea suddenly occurred to her that the able and careful maids by no means can do the work for Him as well as she can. She has kindly but firmly sent the maids off, in order that they should devote themselves to other duties in the houses, the gardens and the kitchens.

This was a bit hard for them. Through Yasoda’s bidding they felt defeated. But the serving, knowing power of Love let them know that it is more precious to serve *those* who serve Him directly, than to think that the aim of life could be achieved by serving Him directly. This insight is not the result of reflection. It is their nature to think and feel like that. But there is *one* grief in their hearts. Yasoda had made clear to them, that they were not allowed even to be near, and she had sent them off to attend to their duties at far-off places. They know why. Yasoda will exert herself and feel somewhat exhausted. If they were close at hand, they would have come hurrying up to the spot and with affectionate force deprived her of her churning-stick. Yasoda’s intention, that she herself should do everything for Him, would come to naught. She has sent them far away. She will exert herself to the utmost. They feel sorry for her; but they must obey the order from the beloved Child’s loving mother. Yasoda’s words are unusually severe, but the maids know that they only constitute the armour, behind which Yasoda’s soft heart is hiding. She wants to protect herself in order to avoid falling a prey to the loving words of the maids; their wish to relieve her of her chores.

The mysterious power that forms Krsna’s and His Own co-actors’ plays, the lila-sakti, has given Yasoda the impulse - almost against her will - to send off all the maids. So things have come about in such a way that she stays alone in the house with the Child.

Carefully she tiptoes up to His bed. The Child rests on a shimmering white cloud-bed, sturdy but yet softer than the soft petals of a blue lotus. - A shining treasure. His body shines like the first sunlit clouds of the rainy season; like a blue pearl, whose brilliance wholly radiates from its centre. His lotus eyes have not yet opened. Calmly breathing, He is still asleep. She strokes Him gently and lays Him down in the middle of the cloud-bed, so that this vivacious Child, should He suddenly wake up, might not fall out of the bed on to the floor. Unconcerned she can attend to her first duty. On the veranda, the big earthenware jar, filled to the brim with soured milk, is already prepared. She walks out and begins churning. From that place she can keep an eye on the sleeping Child quite well. She sets the big whisk in rotating movement and hums short, festive songs to herself, which deal with Him and His childish, yet amazing heroic deeds. Songs, that the women in Vraja use to sing and songs that spontaneously form in her mouth. She sings, because today she wishes that the ever restless Child, for His Own good, will be fast asleep and sleep a little longer than usual, so He will be fully recovered from the exhaustion from His pranks. When she sings these songs she remembers the enchanting plays of the Child, ever since His birth:

“Oh You, ornament of Nanda’s (lord of Gokula) family,  
You, wealth and fruit of Happiness,  
You, virtue of the people of Vraja.  
Your being, Your play are the joy of our eyes,  
because of You, the whole of Vraja is in the state of joy!  
Your birth means feasts, full of bliss, full of joy.  
Your playing breath was the death of Putana,  
and a blessing for us all in Vraja.  
The demons ‘Whirlwind’ and ‘Ox-cart load’,  
were destroyed, but You were saved by God.  
You, who so cleverly crawl about  
on hands and knees on the yard,  
to the joy, to the rejoicing of those who are Yours.  
Your dance in the play, oh –  
such a skill You manifest,  
oh You, foremost of all dancers!  
In the peculiar rosy little hands of Yours,  
You hold on to the playing little tails of the calves,  
in the happy line – where You run in the dust.  
Very witty in squabbling and lies and in hiding Yourself,  
when the women are cross with You, due to your pranks.  
As they love You, they come to me, complaining.  
Oh Krsna, oh Krsna, be forever Your mother’s joy,  
be, Krsna, forever, my happiness!  
See that You grow to greater and greater plays and deeds,  
for the joy of Your mother.  
A very peculiar sight – of cosmic worlds,  
as by the force of Visnu – You showed me.  
May happiness och prosperity come to us,  
through worship of Narayana.  
May You have an immortal body,  
free from illness and pain,  
Oh Krsna, You treasure, You treasure of my love!”

She sings while she whisks. Cautiously peering, while He pretends to be asleep, He sees her at a distance. - The mother! A woman of late middle age, of medium height, her dress mildly shining like a pale rainbow. The colour of her skin is similar to His, just matter in its luster. Her dress is tied together round her sturdy hips with a silk ribbon. She wears a flower garland in her hair, tied up with selected ribbons. In her hands, she holds a soft, but strong piece of string, by means of which she keeps the big whisk in motion. The bangles round her arms ring. The bracelets round her wrists sing like intoxicated bees, round her deft, emerald green lotus hands. Slowly, the earrings dance in pace with her swinging figure. It is a heavy chore, making the butter; but tirelessly, her arms and hands pull at the string. She is almost a bit tired, already. But can there be fatigue when she churns fresh butter for Him? Light beads of perspiration glisten at her forehead and cheeks. The white jasmine flowers in her hair begin to loosen. Her necklace dances at her bosom, full and heavy with gifts for her beloved Child. Her neck, and the back of her neck, glisten by the heat of her bodily movements, and the sturdy hips tremble somewhat.

She looks at her chore and her Child at turns. Thick drops of soured milk have fled the earthenware jar in their madness and arrived at her dress. What does it matter? Every effort for His sake is a joy and every stain an ornament. She really would have taken offence at these stains, had it not been for her churning for Krsna’s sake.

Yasoda whisks the soured milk for Him, who through His being, His charm and His lila whisks and excites the heart and mind of those who see Him or hear about Him.

For a long time, He secretly peeps from a long distance. He knows it to be her joy, to exert herself for His sake. He does not want to deprive her of that joy. But is she not exerting herself too much? Already, as a token of her love, some flowers have fallen from her hair down to the ground, as if stars had fallen from heaven and kissed the sanctified earth, where the Divine Mother, the embodiment or figure of eternal motherly love, in unflagging service for Krsna exhausts herself up to the point of self-oblivion.

But Krsna has a compassionate heart. God always hastens to the spot when some of His Own co-actors, for His sake, unaware of the pain, painfully exerts himself. And besides - in her reflecting and pondering upon Him, has she not noticed that He is already awake? Pretending to cry a little, He gives a sob, leaves His bed and runs quickly up to her. Out of breath, He stretches His tiny limbs, still caught in His sleep, and rubbing His eyes with His tiny hands, He suddenly stands at her side. She knows how fond He is of that fresh butter. She exerts herself for His sake and considers herself to be the only one who can make it good enough. But is all this more important than He is? Imploringly, He looks at His mother. He must call her attention to Himself. He stands there looking as if He were simply

starving. Finally, He seizes the whisk and checks its movement. “Ma, at once! Do not make Me sad. Give Me milk, let Me drink from your breast. Otherwise – I will smash the earthenware jars in the storage room to pieces!” He must threaten her – she overstrains herself – and must she not serve Him as He wants to? Can someone believe that he can serve Him and do what is best for Him at his own discretion and ignore His direct wish? Is it really possible that she can forget Him, for the butter intended for Him. She does so. She is so absorbed in her service for Krsna, but this is not enough to make Him satisfied; He has come to her by Himself; she must give Him what He wants!

She is not capable of anything else. The sight of Him, His captivating words have enchanted her. Lightly, He stamps His tiny feet on the ground. The exquisite rings round His delicate ankles ring clearly. He really looks very tired and hungry. His face is so thin, His black locks hang imploringly on His bright forehead. She obeys and lets the string of the whisk rest. She takes Him into her lap and gives Him her overflowing breast. As the cataka bird feeds on the heavy drops from the clouds in the rainy season, Krsna lies at His mother’s rich breast.

It is not that she obeys Him, because she has experienced Bhagavan’s majesty and grandeur. It is His charm, His loveliness and His roguish game, to play the part of the starving, that she experiences so deeply that she cannot do anything but conform to His wishes. It is so strange that in His tiny hands He can check the quickly rotating whisk in its revolving movement. It is so charming when He even threatens to smash the earthenware jars into pieces. She is completely under the spell of the experience of God as the fullness of charm, loveliness and unconcerned exhilaration. But her eye falls on the milk, intended for Him, which stands over there, over the fire. A breath of air has kindled the slow fire to a vehement flame. The steaming milk will boil over and be ruined. She cannot bring Him along that close to the fire. There is nothing to be done about it, even if He is just in the middle of His drinking the coveted milk from her breast, she must leave Him there and hurry away. “Oh Krsna, You dear Child! Have patience just for a moment. Watch the earthenware jar with the soured milk. I will quickly look to Your milk and will be back in a moment!” Quickly she hastens away and leaves the disappointed Boy behind.

11

***Second Part***

Her heart is fully absorbed in Him. Out of motherly love heavy drops run from her overfull breast, drops, whose essence finds its fulfillment in Krsna’s lotus mouth and close to His flowerwhite teeth. Helplessly, the milk streams on Yasoda’s noble dress.

How is it possible that she leaves Him again? Is she unaware that He can never have enough when He is lying at her breast - and today she leaves Him when He is still hungry?

Why does she proudly exclaim that she can do it better than the maids? There is not one of them who at the slightest wish from their mistress would not instantly be on the spot like lightning. Why does she forget that it is more important to fulfil His immediate wishes, than to worry about that which in her opinion is meant for Him only later. The fire is dangerous, and for that reason she did not bring Him along. But today He had come to her by Himself, and she should not run out on Him on any account!

Nevertheless, what is her fault? She must bear the displeasure of the Child. He is still too small to be able to understand the importance of the duties for His sake. Krsna knows quite well that her behavior is an expression of the great love, as all scolding and threatening from His Own elder co-actors, when in His merry plays He goes beyond the bounds, within which they want Him to keep Himself - for His sake. But today He has asked for something which is very dear and precious to *Him.* Deprived of that, He gets angry.

Tears of rage fill His eyes. His lips tremble. Biting His lip with His tiny teeth, He picks up a stone from the ground and with His angry hand He breaks the earthenware with soured milk to pieces. To His great disappointment there is no butter there. For so long and with such great difficulty she had churned. For that sake she had forgotten even Him, who had been lying on the little bed waiting, expecting her to come to Him, in order to give Him her breast. Can the hardship of the bhaktas please Him, when it does not bear any fruit? What is then the use of all efforts?

The earthenware as an instrument for the effort for His sake is completely broken to pieces. With His stone He breaks the big pieces to small bits of shards. Let the bhakta start all over again, with better tools, and next time produce a better result of his effort.

In long streams the soured milk flows along the floor of the veranda, viscous as the feeble, futile effort of someone who wanted to serve God, but actually blameless, was incapable of doing it.

The sight of the result of His anger could not calm Him down. But there is a little fear in this anger. As we know, He is God in the capacity of the Child. Yasoda’s motherly love keeps Him completely under its spell. To Him, the Child, it is an experience of happiness to subordinate Himself to her, the Divine Mother. He is fully absorbed in the role of being the Child. What will she say when she catches sight of the new boyish prank He has now been up to? Fear and worry have crept into His heart. But the experience of fear cannot appease His anger. When the result of the service does not reach Him in that way, He Himself must see to it that He gets it, and steal it!

Prudently and quickly He goes to a place where there are no people and where no one can observe Him - to the storeroom, where the fresh, clarified butter (ghi) is stored. Through a small window which He cleverly opens He climbs into the room and helps Himself properly. Hey, that mitigates His anger. Is the butter not the fruit of today’s effort, still, it is the result of the effort from some previous day. He knows that His Own co-actors keep the fruit of their labor for His sake at a very secret place. No one should know where it is placed, and no one - except Him ̮-will enjoy it. When, from within, through the power of His lila, He has made His Own co-actors serve in another way, then He will come Himself - when the bhakta not in the least expects it - and rob what is His and what the bhakta has prepared for His sake. He loves to taste this fruit of serving, knowing Love at the time when the bhakta is unaware of it. The fruit is sweet, the result of the bhaktas’ efforts is abundant. This *must* mitigate even His strong anger.

Now His anger is appeased. But the fear, which out of love for His mother has crept into His heart, has neither reached its full maturity, nor has it seen its object, the mother, face to face. His noble deeds are misdeeds in the eyes of His mother. He must flee. He, Whom everyone in all the worlds fear, in so far as He is the Fullness of majesty, grandeur and glory, He, Whom the time and all beings urged by it *flee,* and in Whose field of vision Maya, the cause of all the world systems in the shape of their efficient force and their substance, only ashamed and from afar dares to appear; *He* flees for fear of His mother!

Whenever He wants something, everything must become His friend. Once more a window on the next wall becomes a friend. What a sight! “What will mother say if she catches Me here?” The mere thought of it makes His eyes roll and flee, as if they sought shelter in His ears. “Is she coming? No, not a sign.” Carefully, He closes the little wooden window behind Himself.

How wonderful! There is a mortar. And outside the tall window the funny young monkeys swing in the tall trees. He turns the mortar upside-down, which now offers a comfortable seat. With one’s hand one can now reach into the earthenware with ghi and feed the monkeys at pleasure.

Khala, the mortar, is a villain. But when He turns a villain upside-down, even the villain can be engaged in His service. In that way He made the mortar, Udu-Khala, to His seat. And the monkeys? They are munis, great seers who are in charge of specific, profound parts of the Vedas or srutis. As the result of their asceticism, practiced for Krsna’s sake, and their bhakti they may now participate in this Divine graceful lila as monkeys and with their own eyes see the Absolute Truth and also please Him with their lovely pranks. Vraja-Krsna, the most profound secret or mystery, Who was unavailable to them as wise munis, now sits in front of them on the mortar and distributes the clarified butter to them. He cannot do anything else. He must share the fruit of His Own co-actors’ efforts for His sake, with those who so faithfully serve Him. Can there be a greater mercy, than to be allowed to eat of *that* which He Himself has eaten of so abundantly, and so generously distributes to them?

It is His, what He distributes. The joy of handing out the fresh butter to His funny monkey friends has almost made Him forget that His mother probably already must be on His track.

***Third Part***

Yasoda has removed the milk from the fire and with quick steps hurried back to the place where she had left Krsna. She looks at the scene of His deeds; the small bits of shards from the earthenware, the revealing piece of stone, the Child’s footprints - she knows Who has given vent to His anger here. She smiles. How thoroughly He has worked! How sad and angry He must have been when she left Him. It was difficult even to her to remove Him from her breast when He was still hungry. And yet - she must be angry at Him. He must learn to handle His Own earthenware with soured milk and butter cautiously. He must learn that even anger cannot go so far as destroying that which belongs to Him. Anger and laughter blend in her heart, as anger and fear had blend in His heart. He is *my* Child. Where He is not *willing* to understand, I must treat Him with severity. He must learn to obey. She takes a stick in her hand; not that she could ever think of wanting to strike Him, but because this time, by infusing fear, she wants to give more weight to her words. But when she stands there thoughtfully, prepared to set off, following His footprints, it is as if she hears an invisible voice from the sky: “The little Child Honeythroat was thirsty and has destroyed this lotusbud, not yet moistened with ripe honey. At its bottom the Child found no honey. Then Honeythroat went to another lotus and found plenty of honey there. And now Honeythroat is busy generously giving away the most delicious honey. You are very skilled and have appeased the wildly upset boiling milk, but only when you know how to appease the anger of the Child, you will really be worthy of glory and praise.”

Smilingly she is off and attentively she follows His footprints of soured milk. Cautiously and without causing any noise she opens and shuts the doors, until she sees the peaceful picture from afar - sitting on the mortar He feeds the young monkeys with the carefully prepared and concealed, clarified butter!

Her name is Yasoda. Through her, Krsna’s greatness is known. Through her, it becomes evident that He, Krsna, God in His capacity as Fullness of charm, is so under the spell of her unselfish, motherly eternal love that for her sake He fully knows Himself as Child, and sitting on the mortar, over and over again anxiously keeps a lookout to see if the mother follows His track. She carefully steals forward from behind. But a thief has hundred eyes, a follower only two. When the monkeys, who already have had enough to eat, perceive the mother equipped with the stick, they swing by the tall window up to the branches hanging down from the trees, and escape. Krsna flees for dear life. It had been hard enough for her, to have to dispense with the sight of Him during the short moment she had to see to the boiling milk. Does He now want to escape her once again? He always loves to hide Himself. Without striving and searching with all might of one’s being, one cannot properly love Him in a knowing and serving manner. All that is noble, demands maturity, inner strength and self-sacrificing perseverance. Not only Himself, but also the path of serving knowing Love He has hidden in an ingenious manner in the

15

Revelation of the holy eternal Words. What can a person divine of the mystery that is the Fullness of charm, who is not even prepared to learn that the slightest breath of unconscious thinking of oneself and one’s own happiness is like an impervious layer of clouds, which totally obscures the little spark of light, the atma, and which not passes through any light from the Divine Sun of serving, knowing Love? He even tries to evade His Own co-actors, who from eternity live through that power of the Divine Sun; who fully are power of the Divine Sun, in order that even greater dynamics of the serving, knowing Love, and even greater joy will burst forth when they find Him. Even He, in His capacity as Fullness of charm, is first to be found when He wants to. And when He is unwilling, He even escapes the eyes of His Own co-actors, eyes, saturated with serving knowing Love.

She knows that His deeds and misdeeds only make Him more dear in her heart. But outwardly she expresses anger and dislike and wants to infuse fear into Him, because she wants His own good. Her only worry is that His thoughtless exhilaration will do Him harm. But can He ever be the object of indignation and resentment, even if it is just pretended indignation and resentment? Before her indignation and anger are exhausted, she must search, walk and run, and yet be unable to reach Him.

The manner in which He runs away is so enchanting. She is barely capable of keeping up the appearance of anger. Quickly, she runs after Him. Her clothes flutter, the flowers in her hair fall out. She calls out to Him: “Oh, You thief, what are You heading for?” But He is the one who runs fastest. She has the stick in her hand. That is too much for Him. The stick means an insult to His self-esteem and His honour. It is as if a heavy, slowly westward drifting cloud wanted to catch up with a small, by strong winds drifting, eastward fleeing little wisp of cloud. He flees on a way, where the mother cannot follow Him so quickly. But on roundabout ways she hurries along in order to get hold of Him from another direction. As long as He runs without looking back, she is unable to catch up with Him. But when He looks round, roguishly and at the same time full of fear, He loses time and she is within an ace of seizing Him.

“Stop, stop!” she cries, almost unable to breathe. But can He already yield to her? Can anyone give Him orders, when He does not want to? And yet, such a joy! Yogi-s, who have prepared their mind in hard training during a long life, filled with asceticism, self-discipline and study, from them God, in the capacity of Fullness of omnipotence and majesty, escapes, as He is quicker than the fastest thought. When He is unwilling, neither thought nor word can reach Him. But she, the noble Yasoda, lets herself be wholly filled with the sight of the Fullness of charm and with her body she follows Him, this impulsive, exhilarated cloud of sweetness, and she can almost catch up with Him!

He is clever, and knows how to make use of the terrain to His advantage. She calls out: “King You are, oh Krsna, King of the cunning, the shrewd and the treacherous!” Could there be a greater praise of God? Are there any tricks that He does not utilize, when it comes to challenging His Own co-actors to even greater self-sacrifice, as far as to their being in despair and on the verge of breakdown?

But does He not go too far now? Does He not tire her out too much? He looks round quickly. He must not give in before her pretended anger has melted away completely and she has dropped the stick.

She will strain herself too much, His beloved good mother. Absorbed in His lila as the Child, seized with pity for His mother, He also loses His breath, as if He already was at the end of His strength. Her pity with Him must expel the rest of her anger. She calls out to Him, begging Him to stay. Her heart is moved. But He makes a condition: she must put aside the stick. She breathes heavily. He cries full of fear. She promises to put away the stick. But has she not, only a moment ago, called out to Him: “If You intend to steal in the house, then look closely at this stick!” Now He surrenders, still crying with anxiety, sobbing. With His tiny hands He daubs the black color on His eyelids, mixed with tears, all over His moonface and His eyes roll, full of fear and helplessness.

Krsna says in a pitiful voice: “Ma, but you must not strike Me!” How could she! His charming appeal and His compliance, His sweet movements have won her heart long ago. She knows that it always ends in *His* triumph. But peevishly she gets at Him: “Oh, You Foremost of all thieves!” Oh, yet another praise! But He *is* The Thief of all thieves. He steals the heart from all those who truly hear about Him. He steals the mind from all those who only know Him as the Fullness of majesty, glory and might. From all those who are to be seized by the knowing serving Love, He steals all things, and the attachment to those things - when they hinder the loving service of Him. From the wise, those who are fully free from ignorance of the nature of their own atmas, He steals the peace and self-assurance, the peace in experiencing the imperishable unity with the tranquil light of Brahma, and the peace in merging into this aura encompassing His transcendental form. From those who live in the cognizance of the nature of the atma, He steals their revelling in the clarity of the joy, that their own atma is. He deprives them of the joy that is implied in the pure lightening of the Paramatma in the mirror of their pure atma. He deprives the bhaktas and those who want to become their equals, not only the attachment to the things of the world of change - and by that the bitter disappointment, necessarily following such attachment - but also every interest in the deliverance from the agony of ignorance. He is HARI, the Thief of all thieves.

“If I am a thief, then all your ancestors are, too!” Yes, all her parents and relations by their paternal love for Him have, long since, stolen His heart, and they steal the heart of all those who hear about this Love, that consists of Knowledge, and they awaken the yearning, sometime in future, to be allowed to serve those noble ancestors and relations of Yasoda.

“Tell me, how did the earthenware break?” - “Through the punishment of the Almighty.” - “Who gave the monkeys ghi?” - “He Who created the monkeys.”

The mother hears His answers. She smiles when she thinks about the profound meaning - and yet, to her this is nothing but the sweet prattle of the Child. She threatens and scolds Him. There is no use trying to speak nonsense. His misdeeds deserve a just punishment. She scolds Him, to Whom - in His capacity as Fullness of omnipotence and glory - the wise, at a distance, reverently praying, and with folded hands, sing their hymns. Every word that she speaks bears evidence of the profundity of her experience of Him, this Fullness of charm, and that she is in no respect disturbed, neither by His deeds nor by His words - which clearly and distinctly reveal the Fullness of omnipotence to be present in Him, at the same time. In Vraja, He experiences the fullness of His Own serving, knowing Love for Himself, for God, not as the Lord, but as the Child. It is her tremendous happiness that through her complete lack of reverence and submission, she only more and more intensifies His Self-experience as the Divine Fullness of charm, sweetness and unconcerned exhilaration.

Such a joy for Dhara, who has merged into *one* person with Yasoda, and now may serve Him! Fully absorbed in this secret of Yasoda’s Love for God, He can -He must - for her sake, be even more exhilarated, be the Child, even more.

“Ma, did I commit a fault? Why are you so angry?” Since long, she is not angry any more. Actually, she has never been angry, for His sake she has only tried to be. But He cries and sobs, and stronger and stronger the fullness of charm breaks through.

“Ma, you ran so fast to save the milk, quite unaware of your ankle rings accidentally hitting the earthenware, so that it broke to pieces. Why do you scold me? It is none of my doing, the monkeys coming here to steal, is it? I did my best. Every time I tried to catch them.”

Surreptitiously, He takes a rapid glance at His hands - yes, they are quite clean. During His long flight He has skillfully wiped His hands on the walls. Not a trace of ghi could be found on His hands. “When I saw you with the stick in your hand, I ran away, full of fear. You had told Me to stay by the earthenware with soured milk, and now you are angry, because I did not stay there. But why are you threatening Me with the stick, Ma, why are you so merciless?”

Still, He is filled with fear and His little body trembles with anxiety. His tiny hands shake in her big hand. Oh, how terrified He was, when she caught up on Him from behind and seized Him. - Yes, it was quite impossible! He is too small to break the heavy earthenware with a piece of stone all by Himself. In her hurry, carelessly, she must have broken it herself. Someone must have left the heavy mortar upside-down after this piece of work. He is still too small to be able to do this. Maybe He actually just wanted to catch the little monkeys in His act of folly. In my zeal I probably have done Him wrong. But she must not admit this to Him. He is *her* Child. He must learn to obey. He must be disciplined. She must behave as if she considered everything to be His fault, and His misdeeds, after all.

Dissembling and lie, for Krsna’s sake, as expressions of unalloyed Love and Knowledge of God as Fullness of charm; the sincerity and truthfulness of the most high-minded man, either as an act of virtue in order to attain peace and salvation after death; or in order to please God as the Fullness of majesty - these three are related to each other as the sun, a miserable little oil lamp, and the moon.

“Your little talkative mouth is like a king among all clever and shrewd evasions. You Thief of all thieves! You are a human child, but when You played with the little monkeys You were infected by them and now behave like a monkey Yourself!”

That was too much! Had His persuasive powers been in vain? Did the power of the Divine Play want to initiate an even deeper experience of Himself as the Fullness of charm?

Full of fear – and at the same time striking new terror into her – He prattles: “Ma, then I will take to the woods, like a little monkey, and stay there.”

19

***Fourth Part***

That gave her something to think about! “The Child has its own pride. Actually, He can take to the woods, because I called Him a monkey. I have sent all my maids away, although they wanted to stay. But why should I call on them? No one can bring up his own child as its own mother. But there is plenty to do in the house. For His sake all my multiple duties are waiting. If I let Him loose, who knows, maybe He takes to the woods, after all. I had better bind Him.”

She takes Him by the hand, and while she strides across the courtyard she sees the heavy mortar, lying on the ground, thin in its middle, mighty and wide in its ends. That comes in handy for her. To bind the Child with a soft, strong band! Then, He can neither hurt Himself, nor run away!

“Now, You listen, You little thief! Your rolling eyes enchant everyone that sees You. But Your anxiety and your tears are of no use in front of Your mother! You do not listen to my words. I will bind You, then go back into the house, and quickly set about my duties. Bound to the mortar, You can manifest Your power and steal what you like!”

“Bind Me?” The mother seems to be fully determined. In anxiety and anger He looks around, and in a shrill voice, filled with tears, He cries: “Ma, Ma Rohini! Ma, where are you? Where is Balarama? Come, come quickly!” But Rohini and Balarama are not in their house in the northern part of the courtyard. They are off, and His cry cannot reach their ears. Rohini loves Him more than her own child. She would certainly have protected Him from being bound. If Balarama had been there, the mother would have told *him,* the one who is a little older, to look after Him, as she usually does, quite often.

But other women in the neighboring houses hear His call. But only those, upon whom the power of the Divine Play bestows the Grace to hear His call, because they are needed in the play that follows. One woman after another hasten to the spot. The sight of Him puts them all into a state of concurrent joy and surprise. There He was, the little thief, who every now and then came running into their house, and when believing Himself to be unobserved had stolen butter and sweets, and had played dangerous, funny games with their children. How often had they not come to Yasoda, complaining. But every time, Krsna had knew how to play the truly innocent, so that Yasoda, instead of scolding Krsna, only was disappointed with them. Actually, they had not wanted to complain, by no means. It was their secret joy, when He had stolen into their house, performing His boyish pranks. Every now and then, by stealth, they had observed Him from a hiding-place. Why, they could never take their eyes off His charm. As one day, when He, hands and mouth filled with stolen sweet amusements, saw His reflection in a shiny pillar in the house, and took it for a mate, saying: “Psst! Be quiet! Come, eat half of it, but you must not betray Me.” - Could they ever forget this? How sad they were when they heard that yesterday He had been to the neighbor and performed one prank or other! Oh, why not in my house? They always thought like that, but outwardly they complained, calling Him “thief and “wretch”. Why, He is all to them, and all is

His, and they are all His. This is a spontaneous knowledge, born of this serving, knowing Love, not some kind of reflection, not what we usually call, “to be aware of something”. The fullness of Divine charm keeps them under its spell. They are protected from the knowledge of omniscience and omnipotence, which are always present in this Child. Otherwise, the fullness of charm would be repressed and covered up. Awareness of His omnipotence then would have forced the women to dignified reverence. Since eternity, their atma, their heart, their body, their senses, and all they have, fully consist of Being, Knowledge and Bliss. Since eternity, it is inherent in their being, to knowingly love Him in His capacity as the Fullness of Charm. With every word, every thought, every look, and every deed they serve Him.

There He cries now in His despair. It is Rohini He cries for. Then something very particular must have happened. Once again, He must surely have been up to something! Curiosity is a musty vice in the world of change. But curiosity for Krsna’s sake is an expression of the serving, knowing Love of God. His Own co-actors are insatiable. In every moment, the Fullness of charm *is* quite different. Furthermore, His Own co-actors experience Him - even though they see Him night and day, incessantly - as if they never had seen Him as yet. Just as they, their love and their knowledge are inexhaustible, so is He - according to His Own nature -inexhaustible. At every moment, He is truly new, different, unheard-of, and He can never get enough of experiencing Himself in His Own co-actors as inexhaustible charm.

To the women in the neighboring houses, His repeated cries for Rohini and Balarama are such wonderful pretext for being allowed to hasten to Him. They are well aware of the fact that Yasoda is not in want of maids and female helpers. Without reason, they cannot - for His sake - over and over again leave their own chores and hasten to Yasoda’s house, disturbing her with their visits. But today there is such a lovely pretext; they have heard and observed how one woman after the other in the surrounding houses have run away to Him. Every one of them finds an excuse and a justification for their arrival by the example of the others. Just as disgusting as the mass instinct of the world of change is, just as wonderful is the contagion of curiosity, pretext and self-justification for the sake of Krsna.

Thus, there the mother tightly holds His hand, near to the mortar. His anxiety, His tears, His fear, His unwillingness, and His eyes rolling in anger, His helpless gaze at the mother, sometimes pleading, sometimes seeking relief, and the firm determination in the mother’s features arouse compassion in all the women. And yet, there is the gratification of redress in their hearts, and full of mutual understanding they smile at each other: so, at last, the thief has been caught in his own house! Beholding the mother, their looks say: you did not want to believe us. Today, you yourself have caught Him red-handed in the very act! But they also know: Yasoda loves Him so immensely. Today, it is the Love that makes her so severe. They fully realize that; she cannot do anything else - she must punish Him, however sorry they feel for her, and however great their compassion on the crying Child may be.

From her hair, already in a state of loosening, Yasoda takes a fine silk ribbon in order to put it round His tender body and tie Him to the mortar. Surprisingly enough, the silk ribbon is too short. Quickly, she takes another piece of ribbon, still in her hair, and ties it to the first one. But it is two fingers short. The women look at the Child in amazement. Both were ready to drop with fatigue from the wild run. But what is the good of that! She cannot allow herself to be influenced by His weeping, His helpless look, His childish unwillingness and obstinacy to be bound. She cannot yield to her fatigue. Everything for Krsna’s sake, even if it hurts Him in His want of judgement - and herself infinitely more.

Her eye falls on the women, whom she has not noticed at all, up to now. She asks them to bring fine, soft strings from their houses, strings for the whisking of milk, a big selection of which are always kept in their houses.

One woman brings one piece of string - it is too short. Another one brings another piece of string - still too short. They bring the most exquisite strings, soft and yet strong. How splendidly, at the same time, they can serve Him and His mother! The best in the house is His. Yasoda is clever at binding. All His Own co-actors have the most unsurpassed perfection and dexterity in their service of Him. The women’s speedy departing and arriving attract other women, who hasten there with their small children, bringing new strings, and they rejoice at the opportunity to look at Him so thoroughly and in such close proximity to Him. The children gaze in open-eyed wonder at their Krsna, their leader, their friend and hero. They all feel deeply for Him. But they can hardly grasp what is going on. Who can?

Carefully and quickly, string after string are tied to each other, and yet they are two fingers short, over and over again. The wonderful Child! As long as He does *not* want to, can anyone bind Him then? Every other woman had given in, a long time ago. The women look at each other and say to Yasoda: “Give up! Some secret miracle is brewing. There must be some secret here. The long string of joined pieces reaches round your house but not round the body of the Child!” He is the little Child. Nothing has changed in Him. They can all see that with their own eyes. The strong, long strings cannot bind His tiny body - just as dark, dense masses of clouds cannot rise above a brave mountain peak.

Mildly smiling, the women say to the mother: “You mistress of Vraja! This thief s charm enchants everyone! His enchanting power even makes the thief of all thieves to tremble. Have you fell a victim to His magic power?”

The mother still sees everything as a strange joke and she replies: “You talk nonsense! I know quite well that you do not express what is on your minds. You pretend to be indignant, but in your heart you are on Krsna’s side, and you just pretend to scold Him as a thief. You certainly have some secret magic power which you use in order to prevent me from binding Him!”

The women answer laughingly: “No, certainly not! We know nothing about such secret powers.”

The mother gives credence to their sincere words. It occurred to her that the wise Garga, who had held the little Child in his arms and given Him His name, had spoken of a great Divine power that would always be close to the Child. “It is probably this power that prevents me from binding Him. The Child knows nothing about this. And while she looks at the still crying and downhearted Child, she becomes more and more firm in her intention. He is my *Child!* If I let Him triumph today, He will never learn to behave with dignity, as befits the child of the king of Vraja. - At last He will only hurt Himself. With her eye she orders still more strings to be brought, and yet more eagerly she sets about her task.

He Himself is the only and true binding, the Friend of all. How can a binding bind the one who himself is the binding of all. Since eternity, and through His Own power of experience and knowledge, He Himself as the Fullness of charm has joined everyone in Vraja to a boundless inseparable unity with Himself. On the other hand, He Himself as the Fullness of majesty has joined all His Own co-actors in Vaikuntha to the same kind of unity. In a part manifestation of Himself He, in His capacity as Visnu, through His mere look from afar, has joined all the world systems in the bosom of Maya inseparably with Himself. All atma-s, who in forgetfulness of God self-forgotten wander about in the different systems of worlds, are inseparably united with Him through the Paramatma, the immanent God, who accompanies them all. And yet, He, Krsna, the Fullness of charm, is the Child and she is His mother. She must be able to bind Him, if she only endeavors hard enough!

She experiences how all the strings are insufficient. Even as the Fullness of charm He never ceases to be the Fullness of endlessness, which makes its appearance only occasionally. Here it appears, however, but the fullness of charm and the serving, knowing Love for Him is too strong; they enchant His mother. She does not experience the fullness of boundlessness and majesty. He is fully the Child. But even as a Child He is the boundlessness to the full; unlimited of time and space and consisting of Being, Knowledge and Bliss. Child and boundlessness, both at the same time. Yasoda under the spell of the serving, knowing Love for the Fullness of charm, and He under the spell of this Love - then there is no possibility of perceiving His boundlessness. When and as long as He does not *want* to let Himself be bound, His boundlessness is manifested, and that is the reason why she does not succeed in this very simple task of binding.

Since long, the women have abandoned the hope that His mother might be victorious. It is not for fear that they obey the mistress of Vraja and quickly bring forth an ever greater amount of new strings; no, they have been smitten by Yasoda’s eagerness and are filled with excitement to see how the matter now will end? It is serious. Dumbfounded and amazed, the little boys look at the scene. It is their triumph! Even when He cries and is helpless, still, their Krsna is always the great hero. The women look seriously at the pains their mistress takes, and yet they smile in their hearts, because with their eyes they drink the Boy’s charm, thereby fulfilling the meaning of their eyes. But they cannot laugh openly. For Krsna’s sake they always have to respect His mother, their mistress.

23

Yasoda is almost at the end of her strength. And yet her eagerness does not yield. Krsna sobs, as the mother has not yet abandoned the will to deprive Him of His freedom of play. His playmates cry out of pity for Him.

Since long, the flowers have fallen out from Yasoda’s loosened hair. Due to the strain she is completely out of breath, her body shivers, bathing in perspiration. She almost feels as she were defeated by her Child. But she must not give in. Her eagerness grows more and more; yes, it is as a Divine enthusiasm in her. “Even if it might cost me my life; I must do everything I can do for Him and I must bind him!” The others stand there with wide open mouths. How will it end?

With His eyes bathing in tears He has a glance at His mother: The good mother, she has reached the end of her strength. In joy she has taken on the most extreme effort for His sake, because she loves Him so much. A thought, a ray of His Grace - He gives His consent - She may bind Him. She did not hesitate to give her *last* strength. Only such love can bind Him. To be bound by her is so easy, when He wants it Himself. As long as He did not want to be bound, the fullness of boundlessness and majesty was manifested. Even now, it is present, but it has ceased to be active.

***Fifth Part***

The strings had been two fingers short. His unwillingness impelled the power of the lila to manifest the unboundedness, the boundlessness of time and space, which the Child always is. His willingness impels the power of the lila to make the unboundedness, which the Child always is, unmanifested. He was not willing to let Himself be bound, until His mother, exerting herself to the utmost, was at the end of her strength. Only such exertion evokes His Grace.

Such is the life and endeavor of all those who, seized by the serving, knowing Love, want to serve His Own co-actors and Him - *endeavor to the utmost, and His Grace. Without* those two conditions, all service of God and thereby all will to Knowledge and Love are in vain. This is not only valid for His Own co-actors at the highest level, those who play with Him perpetually in the realm of fullness of charm, sweetness and unconcerned exhilaration, but at *every* level.

It is the mother’s happiness to be allowed to completely exhaust herself for His sake, in incessantly increasing fervor be allowed to lavishly spend herself for Krsna’s sake. Krsna’s happiness is to experience the strength in His Own co-actors’ serving, knowing Love for His sake. Through them He experiences the inexhaustible depth in Himself as the Fullness of charm, sweetness and unconcerned exhilaration to the highest possible degree, when, in spite of the manifestation of the full boundlessness, which He as a Child always is, under the spell and influence of this knowledge of God as the Fullness of charm, this boundlessness is not perceived at all. Can there be a greater happiness than to be bound by His mother?

She bound Him to the mortar, He, Who has neither inside nor outside, round Whom a bond never can be bound. To Him there is no earlier and no later, no past and no future. In relation to time and space and to His substance He is boundless, endless eternity. He is *all* there is, because He is boundless Being, boundless Knowledge and Bliss. Yes, the world of His realm, His Own co-actors, His Love, all is He Himself. The shadow, i.e. all there is in our world, *never* touches Him or His Own co-actors or anything at all in His realm. Even the strings He is bound with, just as the houses, the flowers and the animals fully consist of Knowledge, fully consist of Bliss, and it is for that reason they finally can bind Him.

All being is founded in Him. And hence He is called: “That Being, which is not dependent on anything, which never needs something else beyond Its Own Self.” He is the *Two-less, the One without a second* (advaya). Human thinking and striving can never seize Him, thus He is called “Adhoksaja”. His Being, His Form never consist of that substance, from which the world systems in the universe originate; thus He is called “Avyakta”. He is called “Martyalinga”, since He, as the Fullness of charm, is two-armed, i.e. has the characteristics of a human being, though He never *is* a human or possesses a human, mortal body. The expression “He has the form of a human being”, implies that the form of man resembles *Him,* as the shadow resembles the light. But He does not *have* the form of man. - Since eternity, Yasoda has the eternal maternal love for Him, though she never *is* His mother. Though originating in *Him,* nevertheless, she has the knowing Love for Him, the Fullness of charm, as if she were His mother. As a Child He subordinates Himself to this knowing Love, experiencing Himself as the Fullness of charm. She binds Him, as if He *only* were the Child, as if the ever present boundlessness in Him did not exist at all, as if He had an inside and an outside! Her eternal knowledge of God is not to be mistaken in that respect, since, *at the same time,* He is *the unity of the - to our thinking - impossible opposites:* Child *and* boundlessness!

He, who is the Origin of all, He, who is always independent, He fully yields to His Own co-actors’ serving, knowing Love. In the form of His Own servant He gets fully under the power of Himself. Him, to Whom endless world systems and their moulders (Brahma-s) are subservient, He experiences it as happiness, to be bound to the mortar by His mother. *This* Grace, to be allowed to bind Him, came to her share. Through this she proclaims and diffuses God’s glory (Yaso-da), His renown as being fully under the spell of this totally self-sacrificing, serving knowing Love. To bind Him, the boundless Child, is Yasoda’s privilege. *Only* Yasoda is capable of doing that. And to bind Him, the boundless Youth, is Radha’s privilege. *Only* Radha is capable of doing that. Not even the most perfect of His Own co-actors, who, through eternity, in serving knowing Love serves Him as the Fullness of majesty, glory and might, is capable of doing that. Not even Laksmi, Narayana’s most beloved sakti, who never leaves God as the Fullness of omnipotence, can ever share the Grace that Yasoda receives. The serving, knowing Love for the Fullness of omnipotence excludes the experience, service and knowledge of God as the Fullness of charm. It has to be like this, as follows already from the fact that God as the Fullness of omnipotence does not experience Himself as the Fullness of charm. This implies no limitation of Himself, since He is both, the Fullness of omnipotence and the Fullness of charm. And much more than these two. In His realm, He is *always* the fullness, the boundlessness. He is *always* form. At the same time, all of His Own forms of Being in His Own realm are simultaneously present *everywhere,* without mixing with each other. This may be in contravention of the logical laws of poor mankind, but who has told man that the laws of *his brain* are the laws prevailing in God’s realm? The laws we experience as binding upon our empirical world, and which we in immense presumptuousness declare to be universally valid, are laws valid in our universe. They are intended for the atma-s who have turned their backs on God, and by means of a fictitious I, through their mind and body want to experience a world, conditioned by time and space.

Not even the most eminent and noble man is by his own efforts capable of perceiving even an air of God’s realm. Only *the* atma, who is touched by God’s Own power of knowledge, might through this power in the form of serving knowing Love totally exhaust himself in endless exultation to His joy and divine something of God’s secret.

God as the Fullness of charm, sweetness and exhilaration, Yasoda’s Son, is not attainable to those who consider themselves human beings and have not yet grasped that mind, soul and body are nothing but covers, alien to the nature of the atma. He is not attainable to those who dive into the knowledge of the nature of the atma and into the boundless, peaceful light of Brahma, which is the aura or the formless reflection from God’s Own form and thereby from all His avatara-s. As was mentioned above, the avatara-s are those eternal forms of God’s Being who, without the slightest change, “descend”, from the world of space- and timelessness to the world of space and time. In this context, “descend” does *not* imply any spatial direction, but expresses a relation of value.

The Son of the gopi, Krsna, is neither attainable to those who devote themselves to the knowledge of the nature of the atma - who is nothing but a tiny spark of Knowledge and Being - nor to those who experience the substantial unity of their atma and the Paramatma - the foundation of the world, God as the cause of the evolution of the world. In that case the atma disappears in this unity - as a roe deer becomes invisible when it disappears into the woods - without the atma ever losing his identity with himself and without the tiny spark atma ever qualitatively or quantitatively ever becoming God Himself. It is evident, that the knowledge of Brahma and atma does not lead to Him, Krsna, as not even Laksmi, who eternally serves Narayana, God as the Fullness of majesty, is ever successful in her attempts to attain Krsna, the Fullness of charm, the Child of Yasoda.

And yet, everyone could reach Him! When someone has the powerful longing to serve those who serve Yasoda, then his atma - through the power of the God-sent Grace of serving knowing Love for God as the Fullness of charm, which comes to him through the bhakta - is able to reach Krsna in safety and security.

But want, i.e. *not enough* of Love, makes Him unattainable. But the worst shortage of Love is THE DESIRE TO KNOW, THE DESIRE TO EXPERIENCE, THE DESIRE TO PUSH ONE’S WAY FORWARD INTO THE VICINITY OF GOD. This is not only foul selfishness but want of the true will to let oneself be enlightened by the wisdom of Revelation.

The best parts of the Upanishads, Brahma, the creative designer of our world system, Uddhava, Krsna’s close friend; all those who have perceived something of the greatness of the Love for God as the Fullness of charm, and the greatness of those who are His Own co-actors, have prayed for the fortune, to be allowed to be a grain of dust at the feet lotuses of His Own co-actors in His holy realm, to be allowed to touch those feet, i.e. to be allowed to rub themselves with the dust from the feet of those who serve Him, Krsna.

The atma in man, who in endless lives of forgetfulness of God wrongly experiences himself as man, animal or plant; this infinitesimal spark of Knowledge and Bliss, - which he now does not even know himself to be - can he ever in his delusions of grandeur consider himself worthy to be used as a thread in the string used by Yasoda in her binding of the Child!

Is not Laksmi - the most beloved sakti of Narayana, God as the Fullness of omnipotence - a warning example? Since eternity, she is fully conscious of being Narayana’s most Beloved. She Herself *is* Narayana in the form of Laksmi. And yet, all her endeavour, all her wishes are of no use. All her sacrifices are in vain. She cannot abandon the consciousness “I am Laksmi”, and therefore she lacks the desire to serve the gopi-s, Krsna’s most beloved co-actors in Vraja. - In the shadow, which is available to our experience, of the real Vraja, opposite Vrndavana on the other side of the river Yamuna, a little grove is situated, with a little village. At this place in His realm of Vraja, Laksmi once resided, practicing severe asceticism, in order to be able to experience a little bit of Krsna’s greatness - as the Fullness of charm. And yet she was never allowed to cross the river. The power forming the eternal Play of Krsna, kept her afar!

To be able to know the true nature of Vraja, the Grace of the bhaktas is required. From their heart and mouth stream the words consisting of Being, Knowledge and Bliss, words dealing with Vraja. These words reach through the ear of those who long for the true will to be allowed to serve, into their heart, into their atma. According to the willingness to let oneself be enlightened by these words, being Knowledge and possessing the power to awaken real knowledge of God, it can be known what Vraja is, and what constitutes the greatness of His Own co-actors’ Love and service.

God’s Revelation, God’s Grace consists in His bringing about the meeting with the bhaktas. The serving, knowing Love is conveyed in their words, in the Word-form of His Own form, in His realm, in His lila, and in those who are His Own. These words release the atma from his forgetfulness of God and enable him to be *willing* to sacrifice himself in serving, knowing Love.

It is the great Grace of Krsna that the Damodara-lila is conveyed in the Bhagavatam and other Revelations of God’s Word. It is the great Grace that this manifest lila, at first sight, seems to be a lila within time and space, because that which is beyond time and space would be unavailable to us beforehand, if it did not appear as *if it* was enacted within time and space.

The power of the serving, knowing Love is just as boundless, omnipresent and eternally present as God and His realm themselves. Just as the boundless realm, without changing its content in the least, once appeared within the boundaries of the district of Mathura, the serving, knowing Love - unrestricted in its form of Being - makes its appearence through the mouth of the bhakta. Krsna and the secret of His Love touch the heart, by their entering the ear that longs for His service. But the ear that wants to get intoxicated by the words of the lila, is only able to perceive the shadow of these words, and instead of knowledge and true realization, misconceptions and errors enter the heart. The bhakta is the mouth of spring, through which the eternal knowledge of God gushes forth. The ear and heart of those who are longing to serve, is the chalice. The eternal words of His lila are the very knowledge of God, intelligible through the will and power to serve.

***Sixth Part***

Yasoda has performed her marvellous deed. But Krsna has by no means stopped crying. He has let Himself be bound. He is fully the punished Child. The mother looks at her labour. A look of triumph. And to Him, this look is the most beautiful. Why, He wanted to see this look of triumph. Actually, it was not *her* triumph, it was a triumph for Krsna’s sake, and consequently His triumph. Neither the breaking forth of His boundlessness, nor the fact that it was *His* compassion on her exhaustion, *His Grace*, that made it possible for her to be able to bind Him at all, had caused any disturbance in her experience of Krsna as the Fullness of charm.

She glances at the amazed faces of the astounded women, who do not believe their eyes. Finally, she managed to bind Him, after all! She breaks up in order to see to her duties. She looks at Krsna’s little friends and tells them: “Now you look intently at Him! Look after Him properly! If, in some way, He would free Himself, you must send for me at once, understood?” Accompanied by the women she leaves the scene, leaving Krsna, still quietely crying and bound to the powerful mortar, with His friends.

After a short while He stops crying. His roguish countenance brightens up. Can this ridiculous mortar restrict His play? There are the roguish friends, and with a jerk He crawls ahead, amid their cheers, and with all His might He drags the heavy mortar along.

He really cheers up, it does not cross His mind that this binding is a binding. Amid the merry laughter of His friends, He drags the heavy mortar along, first slowly, then faster and faster, passing the house of the parents, and into the path leading to the road of the village. Why, there are two wonderful trees, the stems of which have grown together, resembling a V. It would be a delight, dragging the heavy mortar right up to the trees – and finally, the string will snap by itself, when the heavy mortar remains hanging in the narrow end of this V!

These two trees are no common trees. In the same way as Krsna enters the world of time and space as if He were the Child of His parents, so that the world will not be able to divine that God and His Own co-actors have come, all His co-actors enter as well. Madhukantha = “honey throat” and Snigdhakantha = “sweet throat” are two bards who delight Nanda and all inhabitants in Vraja at the great feasts in Nanda’s realm with their epical songs. Once, two of Rudra’s servants, in pride, had done an injustice to Narada, the one who bestows Divine wisdom. Their hearts were fully dedicated to God, but when the power of the lila so wishes, peculiar things happen, bringing happiness to all beings. As if under a strange impulse, they had trespassed against Narada. Narada blessed them. He gave them a blessing, which the ignorant world conceives as a curse: they would be two inseparable trees, but through Krsna they would once again be put into their former conditions. Even as trees, they would never forget who they are. These two servants of Rudra entered Madhukantha’s and Snigdhakantha’s beings, the two co-actors who became visible in the lila of Gokula in the shape of two trees.

The power of the lila of Krsna, always aiming at fulfilment of the wishes of those who are His Own co-actors, as Narada, intends to fulfil the liberation of these two servants of Rudra as well.

The boys think that Krsna seeks the cooling shade of the two huge trees. Laughingly, He has now arrived there. He crawls between the two stems, but the mortar is too wide and with a light jerk He bumps against the stems, growing as from one root. - A dreadful sound is heard, which penetrates the universe.

It is a sound that plunges all the inhabitants of Vraja into unconsciousness for more than an hour. It has to be like that, because otherwise everyone could have seen what happened: The mighty trees were lying on the ground. In front of the Child, two noble youths stand with suppliant, raised hands, praying for the gift that their lips always may sing His praise; their ear always only hear about Him; their hands serve Him; their mind always think of His feet lotus; their head pay obeisance to His realm, and their eyes behold those who have dedicated themselves to Him.

Their prayer was granted and He confers the gift of serving, knowing Love upon them.

When He had taken leave of them, the two servants of Rudra disappear, going to their own realm, and the bards go to that realm of Vraja (Goloka), which does not become visible in this world.

Krsna has not wanted and not been able to free Himself from the bonds of motherly love, as these bonds are His pride. But, as by pure chance, His mere touch has freed the two trees from all bonds.

Open-mouthed, the boys had seen all this. They had not grasped anything of the words in the song of praise.

Meanwhile, all the others had recovered from the alarm, raised in them by the power of the Play, which had put them in a state - in order to keep them at a distance - that did not let them know anything of themselves for an hour.

Now they all come running. Nanda, the father, Rohini with Balarama and all the women of Gokula, the children and the other inhabitants. Nanda sees the Child. It is tied up! He looks around, frees the Child, puts Him on his knee and strokes Him gently. Where is Yasoda? Has he not just seen her in the crowd of people, quickly hastening to the spot?

Krsna experiences His Own sweetness through His father’s Love for Him. The father understands Him and asks: “But that is terrible! Who on earth has tied You up here?” Nanda knows all too well that the mother has done this, but he also knows that his own participation makes Krsna happy. Krsna looks around, and in His father’s ear He whispers: “Ma has tied Me up!”

Nanda knows how much the mother has been subjected to, knows that she did it only for His own good and that it almost had an unfortunate ending. Everyone knew the two trees. They were strong and by no means decayed. Something fateful has been going on, but as if by a miracle the Child has been saved.

Nanda and the others ask Krsna’s playmates, how it all happened. “A light touch by the Child and the trees fell aside, two radiant youths ...” - All this is nothing but

silly talk of the boys, it is simply not possible! The children must invent all this, they know just as little as we.

On His father’s knee, Krsna keeps everyone fully under the spell of His charm.

Finally the father takes Him down to Yamuna for a bath. There wise brahmans pronounce benedictions upon the Child. Together with Krsna and Balarama the father has his morning meal. In grief, Yasoda keeps herself out of the way. In the evening, Rohini and other women come and tell them that in her distress, Yasoda has fasted all day and out of shame not uttered a word to anyone, silently performing her duties.

Holding the Child in his arms, Nanda asks Him: “Would You not like to go to your mother?” Krsna: “No, I do not want to. I want to stay by you day and night!” Then the aunts, the wives of Nanda’s brothers, ask Him: “But from whose breast do You want to drink?” Krsna: “I want to drink hot milk with sugar candy in it!” Then everyone ask Him: “But with whom will you play and have fun?” Krsna: “With Pa and Balarama.” Nanda asks Him: “Why do You not want to be with Rohini?” Krsna: “She left Me alone and went away.” And He shed a few tears in anger. Then Rohini says: “Why are You so hard on us? The mother suffers without You!” But with His eyes filled with tears, Krsna just looks at His father, giving no reply. With gestures Rohini tells Balarama to go to Krsna and entice Him to come along with him. But Krsna rejects Balarama’s interference, and with His tiny arms He clings to Nanda’s neck, cries and looks imploringly at His father. And God’s charm lays the father completely under a spell.

But the father knows the strength of Krsna’s love for His mother. In order to entice this love, hidden behind His rejection, He shows the Child his raised hand: “Shall I punish the mother?” But that was more than Krsna could bear. Imploringly, He keeps a firm hold of His father’s hand. Then Nanda says: “Krsna, as things are now with Your mother - she does not eat and grieves - what will You finally do?”

Now He cannot restrain Himself any longer. The great longing for the mother breaks through. Weepingly, He calls: “Where is Ma?” “Where is Ma?” Then Rohini takes Him into her arms and hastens into the house to Yasoda. Oh, how quick He is. When He is set loose, He immediately rushes at the mother and clings to her neck. The mother is totally overwhelmed, clasping Him to her bosom. He weeps and sobs, and all the women around cry. “He has escaped from such a danger, and it could have ended so badly!”

Blest, is the serving knowing Love. She experiences God’s charm and worries and grieves for the sake of the Child, in Whom all boundlessness is present.

The spell of His charm is stronger than her sorrow and grief. She gives Him her breast, and full of bliss He makes up for what He was refused in the early morning. She experiences His charm, and He experiences His charm in her serving knowing Love. - Thereby, all events of the day had almost vanished from her heart. Together with Krsna and Balarama she then sits down to eat, with Rohini and the other women around.

But Nanda has great worries, together with all elders. Many gruesome things had happened at this place. Is it because the town Mathura and the evil king Ka£sa with his demonic friends are so close? It is true that Mathura is situated on the other side of the river, but still, it is an unpleasant neighborhood. One never can tell ...

Several years before Krsna’s appearance, they had lived in Nandagrama, at the foot of the hill Nandisvara. Perhaps it would be more advisable to leave this place for Vrnadvana, stay there for a while, and then leave for Nandagrama.

But until they have held a meeting, consulting with each other, and finally, everyone jointly would leave, all measures must be taken, so that Krsna never, not even for a moment, will be left alone. Nanda tells Yasoda, always to carry the Child in her garment, and not leave Him alone, not even for a moment. Nanda knows: the Child could not be better looked after and protected by anyone else than her. She had already had this thought in her mind, but to Nanda and all the others, to Krsna, and not least to herself, His exhilarated plays were such a source of joy. Everyone finds it hard to deprive Him of His freedom of play. But the great expectation of the journey, the wonderful grove Vrnadvana, and new, new plays make the time up to the departure easy for Him. After this exciting day, it is so lovely to be quite, quite close to each other - she, the mother and He, The God of charm, sweetness and exhilaration.

Now the inhabitants of Vraja have a new name for Him: “Damodara”, i.e.: He who has “dama”, a string round His “udara”, body. In joy and in jest they call Him that.

***Conclusion***

God’s Name, His realm and His Play are eternal. When He, His realm and His Play appear in the world of time and space, then He, His realm and His Play appear in a sequence in time and space. This does *not* imply a breaking through the laws of our world of time and space, on the contrary, the wonder consists in that He and His Play *apparently* follow the laws of our world, *without* being subjected to them *in reality.*

This Play has its own fascination to those who are His Own co-actors and to Himself. It has its own significance to Him and those who are His Own co-actors. It is an eternal Play, appearing in time and space.

In the Play *not* appearing in time and space, i.e. in Goloka, He is the eternal Youth. In that realm Krsna does not manifest the form of the Child. There Yasoda *sees* the Child in Him, in spite of the fact that He *is* the Youth.

But in the manifested lila, i.e. in Gokula, He manifests the form of the Child and she is allowed to bind Him. The Fullness of charm, sweetness and exhilaration, which Krsna is, gets intensified in the manifested lila, and in consequence the serving, knowing Love gets intensified.

As a result of this manifested lila the name “Damodara”, which becomes known during the course of this lila, makes the greatness of Yasoda known, makes herself and Krsna renowned. Krsna fully submits Himself to the serving, knowing Love, fully sacrificing itself for His sake.

His Grace works in the way that He brings about the meeting with the bhaktas. From their lips the words stream, which are identical with the lila itself, words awakening the serving, knowing Love. This serving, knowing Love, which is called bhakti, is Krsna’s Own power of knowledge and experience. Through this power He draws the atma towards Himself and to this power of attraction He succumbs.

The entry to the realm of bhakti is neither the most magnificent human virtue, nor the most noble human character, nor severe asceticism, nor strenuous study of the sanskrit word cover of the eternal Word, nor knowledge of the nature of the atma, but only the Grace of the bhaktas.

To the serving, knowing Love for Krsna, to the Fullness of charm, sweetness and exhilaration, to the mysterious dark Thief of the eyes, heart and senses, leads only *one* form of this serving, knowing Love - i.e. that bhakti, of which Bhagavatam X.9,21 says: “The bhakti for Yasoda, the serving, knowing Love that wants to serve *her,* is the only path to bhakti for Krsna Himself, yes, it *is* the bhakti to Krsna Himself.”

Serving, knowing Love for God is the beginning, the middle and the end; it is its own origin, sustenance and aim. It does not know any “why”, just as He Himself does not know any “why”.

The life of man is enslaved by purpose. The bhakta, however, does not know

33

why and for what purpose he loves God, His Own co-actors and the bhaktas in this serving, knowing manner. Since the bhaktas have this bhakti - which does not originate from man or his atma but flows from God and streams back into Him -Krsna’s Own co-actors and those who are His bhaktas are so dear to *Him,* more dear and precious than His Own Self. That is the reason why the bhakti for those who are His Own, *to Him,* is more dear and precious than the bhakti for Himself.
